### ⛔ WHAT I WROTE ON 9/10 AND WHY IT IS NOW WRONG
My row reads: ***"the FINANCING leg the 4 was set on IMPROVED SPECIFICALLY. OCF a record $23B (+184%); capex/OCF 1.74× → 1.24×; operating cash is compounding faster than capex."***
| | reported | **ex-$11.4B prepayment** |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 OCF | $23.1B | **$11.7B** |
| Q1 capex | $28.5B | $28.5B |
| **capex/OCF** | **1.23×** | **⛔ 2.44×** |
| **Q1 FCF** | **−$5.4B** | **⛔ −$16.8B** |
- ⇒ **⛔⛔ THE 1.74× → 1.24× "IMPROVEMENT" IS AN ARTIFACT. Ex-prepayment it went 1.74× → 2.44× — IT DETERIORATED. And Oracle received NO comparable financing-component prepayments in Q1 FY26, so the +184% OCF growth is substantially the appearance of this line, not operating leverage.**
- ⇒ **★★★★ AND THE ACCOUNTING NAMES IT FOR ME: *"significant financing component"* IS AN ASC 606 TERM OF ART. It means the contract contains an EMBEDDED LOAN and the seller must IMPUTE INTEREST.** ⇒ **the standard itself classifies this as financing — and it lands in the OPERATING section of the cash flow statement.** **That is not my interpretation; it is the label.**
- ⛔ **PERIMETER, BECAUSE THE SCAN'S BULL READ IS FAIR AND I WILL NOT STRAWMAN IT (rule 21b):** this is **real cash, contractual, and cheaper than debt** — no covenants, no rate reset, no refinancing wall. **If customers keep prepaying it is an excellent funding channel.** ⇒ **so the honest uncertainty is RECURRENCE, and ONE QUARTER CANNOT DISTINGUISH a durable new channel from a one-time pull-forward.**
- ⇒ **📌 THEREFORE THE DOWNGRADE IS NOT "PREPAYMENTS ARE BAD." IT IS: **THE REASON I GAVE FOR THE 5 WAS THAT ORDINARY OPERATING CASH WAS OUTGROWING CAPEX, AND IT WAS NOT.** A grade must be revoked when its stated driver is falsified, whatever the name's merits. **ORCL 5 → 4, restoring the grade the financing leg actually supports.**
